claims.statement: `make lint_prose` installs the configured Vale binary and checks either specified files or `src`, excluding `node_modules` and `src/code-samples`; it is a prose style gate rather than a rendering or factual-correctness check.

The changelog-navigation Node tests use an in-memory DOM to verify that the self-hosted changelog indexes only visible stable minor releases, preserves excluded headings, coalesces mutation updates, cleans up on page changes, and falls back to an inline index without a sidebar.

`make export-htmltest` runs Mint export before htmltest; the export requires a Mint CLI with `mint export`, Node 20 or 22, and an Enterprise plan, while htmltest intentionally checks external URLs only because the export omits many pages.

The release-watch `test_evidence.py` suite uses synthetic payloads and source/page text to test evidence parsing, surgical edit validation, and source-claim matching; it does not exercise remote release, GitHub, or Linear integrations.

`make test` runs pytest with Internet sockets disabled while allowing Unix sockets; pytest discovers tests under `tests`, uses automatic asyncio mode, and defaults its asyncio fixture loop scope to a function.

`make lint` runs Ruff formatting and lint checks in diff mode over the configured Python-file scope, `ty check`, and Codespell over `src`, making it a static-quality gate separate from runtime tests and documentation generation.

The main CI workflow runs reusable test, lint, and documentation-link workflows on pull requests, pushes to `main`, and manual dispatch, and separately runs merge-marker, source cross-reference, integration `docs_url`, and generated-provider-overview checks.

`make check-cross-refs` validates source `@[ref]` markers by scanning Markdown and MDX under `src`, skipping code fences, escaped references, generated code-sample snippets, and `node_modules`; unfenced shared OSS references must resolve in every applicable language scope.

`make broken-links-with-anchors` rebuilds documentation and runs Mint's broken-link checker from `build/` with anchor and redirect checking, while `make check-openapi` rebuilds then checks `langsmith/agent-server-openapi.json`; the reusable documentation workflow runs both on Node 22.

`test_url_stub_noindex.py` requires every MDX page with `url:` frontmatter to set `noindex: true` so redirect-only sidebar stubs stay out of Mintlify discovery outputs including `llms.txt` and the sitemap.

CI validates integration `docs_url` metadata with `scripts/refresh_integration_downloads.py --check-docs-urls`; the generator permits HTTP(S) and single-leading-slash site-relative URLs and rejects unsafe schemes, while the generated-file job regenerates and diffs the provider overview rather than accepting manual edits.

The code-sample workflow skips fork pull requests because samples can require secrets, runs changed executable samples on same-repository pull requests and all samples on scheduled/manual runs, and provisions provider credentials, language toolchains, and a pgvector PostgreSQL service.

`make code-snippets` extracts marked snippets and generates MDX without executing them, whereas `make test-code-samples` executes selected or eligible samples; trace-enabled full runs may regenerate snippet MDX after sample execution.
The export htmltest configuration checks external URLs but disables internal paths and hashes because the Mint export is incomplete, so it cannot establish internal navigation or anchor correctness.

`DocumentationBuilder.build_all()` reconstructs the generated tree with Python and JavaScript OSS variants, unversioned Deep Agents Code and OpenWiki content, Managed Deep Agents language variants, shared assets, and npm snippet components; its Markdown processing rewrites language-sensitive links and snippet imports before output is written.

Focused builder tests protect generated navigation topology by checking language-prefix rewriting, single unversioned OpenWiki output, language-scoped snippet imports, and rejection of source symlinks so build collection cannot copy content outside the source tree.

The code-sample runner accepts supported executable files beneath `src/code-samples`, runs each language with its corresponding toolchain, retries recognized rate limits and reports exhausted rate limits as skips, while non-rate-limit failures make the command fail.

Code-sample runs default to four workers but serialize known shared-fixture groups; when tracing is enabled, trace collection is locked and failures collecting a trace warn without converting an already successful sample into a suite failure.

The snippet-MDX generator expands only routable Python or TypeScript agent model strings into provider CodeGroups, preserving embedding and provider-specific chat model identifiers; focused tests enforce those exclusions, language-specific Google provider syntax, and a compatible resolved `@langchain/google` version.

On scheduled or manual code-sample runs, the workflow regenerates snippet MDX only when the run was not cancelled, fewer than 20 samples failed, and trace links changed; it then opens or updates a dedicated trace-refresh pull request containing the trace manifest and generated snippet artifacts.

The `create-an-agent.py` executable sample directs a real LangSmith `Client` to a loopback HTTP fixture, asserts the create and retrieve requests and returned environment values, and removes fixture-only setup and assertions from extracted snippets; it validates local SDK request/response compatibility rather than a live LangSmith agent integration.

The snippet extractor line-parses supported language markers, strips `:remove:` regions, and writes normalized Bluehawk-compatible extracted files; `CODE_SNIPPET_SOURCES` limits processing to supported files below `src/code-samples` and replaces output only for those selected source stems.
`src/docs.json` is the Mintlify site configuration, including navigation, so changes to its navigation or route configuration require generated-site validation rather than only source-level tests.

The code-sample workflow partitions samples into OSS and LangSmith matrix legs, fails when a top-level sample directory has no assigned leg, and limits tracing plus trace-refresh publication to the OSS leg on scheduled or manually dispatched runs.

`CODE_SAMPLE_PATHS` restricts both discovered samples and explicit `FILES` to directories below `src/code-samples`; focused tests verify that a CI product leg can receive all modified paths while retaining only its own files and that out-of-tree filters cannot widen execution.

The builder uses `src/docs.json` navigation routes beneath `oss/python/` and `oss/javascript/` to decide which language copies of shared OSS pages to emit; a route listed in neither language falls back to both copies, and an absent or invalid configuration also falls back to both.

Trace-link collection is limited to source files with exactly one valid snippet ID: the runner stamps that ID in `LANGSMITH_DOCS_SNIPPET`, and the collector requires the same metadata on a root run rather than selecting an arbitrary run from the time window.

The version-claim pull-request workflow checks only changed authored MDX files and fails for a version absent from a successfully resolved registry, while no changed MDX skips setup and registry lookups and a lookup failure is reported as unresolved rather than unpublished.

The egress inventory generator validates schema-versioned public IPv4 `/32` entries, derives a SHA-256 inventory version from canonical address data, and makes `--check` fail when that version or either marked documentation table is stale; a full builder run copies the inventory once to the unversioned LangSmith output path.

OpenTelemetry endpoint tests reject generic OTLP endpoint values that include a signal suffix and collector `endpoint:` values ending in `/v1/traces`; mocked Python exporter tests verify that a signal-specific traces endpoint is unchanged and a generic base endpoint receives exactly one `/v1/traces` suffix.

The deprecated-pattern workflow checks only added lines in eligible pull-request diffs and fails when newly added Python, Markdown, MDX, or notebook content contains `create_react_agent`; it uses read-only contents permission, fetches two commits, and has a five-minute timeout.

The main CI workflow cancels an older run for the same workflow/ref when a newer push arrives; its focused checks have five-minute timeouts, while reusable test, lint, and documentation-link jobs have 20-minute timeouts.

The code-sample runner applies a per-sample timeout controlled by `CODE_SAMPLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, defaulting to 1,200 seconds, and supports Python, TypeScript, Go, shell, Java, and Kotlin execution paths.

The code-sample workflow cancels older runs for the same workflow/ref, gives pull-request runs a 60-minute timeout and scheduled/manual full runs a 150-minute timeout, and waits for its pgvector PostgreSQL service to accept connections before executing samples.
The reusable documentation workflow installs Mint 4.2.1181 on Node 22 and runs broken-link, MDX syntax/component, and OpenAPI checks against the generated documentation tree.

CI's generated-file job regenerates `src/oss/python/integrations/providers/overview.mdx` with `pipeline/tools/partner_pkg_table.py` and fails if the generated file differs, while allowing explicit skips for a named automated package-download update or a `bypass-auto-check` label.
